details: The U.S. Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.75%, a decision anticipated by markets but marked by an unusual four dissenting votes from officials. This indicates a cautious stance by the central bank, which remains concerned about elevated inflation, partly fueled by rising global energy prices. The Fed's position suggests a "higher-for-longer" interest rate environment, leading to ongoing market uncertainty as borrowing costs are expected to remain elevated, generally reducing the appeal of risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US Fed Holds Rates Steady, Signaling Prolonged Uncertainty Amid Inflation & Energy Shocks

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) held its interest rates steady at its April 30 meeting but conveyed a stronger inclination towards a future rate hike, possibly in June. President Christine Lagarde emphasized increased upside risks to inflation and downside risks to economic growth, largely attributing this to the Middle East war's impact on energy prices. ECB projections suggest headline inflation could reach 3.5% or even 4.4% in 2026 if energy supply disruptions continue, prompting markets to anticipate further monetary tightening.
title: ECB Signals Rate Hike Inclination as Lagarde Highlights Intensified Inflation Risks

details: European financial giant BNP Paribas has issued a stark warning regarding the global economic outlook, indicating that scenarios, including oil prices surging to $200 per barrel due to the ongoing Iran war, could precipitate a global recession. The persistent conflict poses significant risks of energy supply disruptions and sustained high inflation, which may pressure central banks to further tighten monetary policy, thereby intensifying the risks of a global economic downturn.
title: BNP Paribas Warns of Global Recession Risk Amid High Oil & Geopolitical Conflict
